n_generators: <int> Number of thermal generators in the fleet.
n_scenarios: <int> Number of equally likely demand scenarios.
T: <int> Number of time periods in the planning horizon.

generators.M: <int> Maximum power output of the generator when running (MW).
generators.m: <int> Minimum power output of the generator when running (MW).
generators.L: <int> Minimum number of consecutive periods the generator must remain on once started.
generators.ell: <int> Minimum number of consecutive periods the generator must remain off once shut down.
generators.RU: <int> Maximum increase in production allowed between consecutive periods while the generator stays on (MW).
generators.SU: <int> Maximum production allowed in the period the generator first turns on (MW).
generators.RD: <int> Maximum decrease in production allowed between consecutive periods while the generator stays on (MW).
generators.SD: <int> Maximum production allowed in the last period before the generator turns off (MW).
generators.c_g: <float> Per-unit cost of power produced by the generator ($/MWh).
generators.c_f: <float> Fixed operating cost paid in every period the generator is running ($).
generators.startup_costs_K: <list[float], length T> Cost of starting the generator after exactly k consecutive inactive periods, for k = 1 to T ($).

demand_scenarios: <list[list[float]], shape [n_scenarios][T]> Power demand for each scenario in each time period (MW).
reserve_scenarios: <list[list[float]], shape [n_scenarios][T]> Spinning reserve requirement for each scenario in each time period (MW).
